newsitem.title: CHINA: China Jan-Feb aluminium imports down yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China Jan-Feb aluminium imports down yr/yr.

text.p: China's imports of unrefined aluminium and aluminium products fell 4.3 percent year-on-year in the first two months of 1997 to 69,224 tonnes, the Shanghai Securities News said on Thursday.
Imports of unrefined aluminium and aluminium products in Feburary 1997 were 31,378 tonnes, down 17.1 percent on the January figure, the newspaper said.

Imports of unrefined aluminium, including aluminium alloys, were 17,922 tonnes in February 1997, and totalled 33,424 tonnes in the first two months of the year, down 22.6 percent on the same period in 1996, it said.

Aluminium scrap imports were 11,350 tonnes in February 1997, up 8.5 percent on the January figure. Total aluminium scrap imports for the first two months of the year were 21,813 tonnes, up 2.9 percent on the same 1996 period, it said.

Russia remained China's biggest source of aluminium, providing 12,353 tonnes in February and a cumulative total of 21,759 tonnes for the first two months of the year, down 6.9 percent on the same 1996 period.

February's aluminium imports from the United States, China's second biggest supplier of the metal, were 9,613 tonnes, for a total of 19,814 tonnes in the first two months, up 21.3 percent on the same 1996 period, it said.

Most of China's aluminium imports came through southern ports in Guangdong province, with 25,744 tonnes in February and a total of 52,948 tonnes in the first two months of the year, down 8.3 percent on the same year-ago period, it said.
Aluminium imports arriving in Shanghai were 5,725 tonnes in February and a total of 11,088 tonnes for the January-February period, up 62.2 percent on the same period in 1996, it said.
